stories.title: New NetScaler Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks Can Knock SAML Deployments Offline
stories.abstract: Citrix has patched a high-severity memory overflow vulnerability, CVE-2026-88779, affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway. This flaw is currently being exploited in the wild, prompting CISA to add it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of edge infrastructure poses a critical risk to network perimeter security and internal access control.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to the latest versions specified in the Citrix security bulletin.

stories.title: Hitachi Energy REB500
Critical Atlassian Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Read Known Files Across 8 Products
Johnson Controls EasyIO FG
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls EasyIO FG firmware versions 2.0b52 and earlier contain vulnerabilities involving hard-coded credentials and improper privilege management. Exploitation allows unauthorized actors to gain full control over affected building automation devices, posing risks to critical infrastructure environments.
stories.why: Compromised building controllers can be leveraged for lateral movement or physical disruption within industrial and commercial facility networks.
stories.action: Update EasyIO FG firmware to version 2.0b52 or later.

stories.title: Google Pauses OSS Product Bug Bounty Rewards After Surge in Invalid Automated Reports
ASOS confirms data breach after “HACKED” in-app notifications
stories.abstract: Fashion retailer ASOS confirmed a security incident after unauthorized push notifications were sent to mobile app users. The messages claimed the company suffered a data breach involving its Snowflake environment, prompting an investigation into the potential compromise of customer information.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to push notification infrastructure often indicates broader account takeover or internal system compromise, posing significant risks to customer data integrity.

stories.title: Rapid7 security advisory (AV26-1004)
stories.abstract: Recent security bulletins highlight critical vulnerabilities across multiple platforms. Rapid7's Velociraptor versions before 0.77.3 contain a permission flaw, Android released its October 2026 patch cycle, and HPE iLO 7 firmware prior to 1.25.00 is susceptible to a user validation failure.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities could allow unauthorized access or privilege escalation, potentially compromising server management interfaces and mobile device integrity.
stories.action: Update Velociraptor to 0.77.3, apply October Android security patches, and update HPE iLO 7 to 1.25.00.

stories.title: Denmark population registry data breach affects 8.8 million people
Nikkei discloses breaches of employees’ Microsoft, Google email accounts
stories.abstract: Japanese media firm Nikkei reported that unauthorized actors gained access to two employee cloud email accounts. The attackers leveraged one of the compromised accounts to distribute approximately 9,000 phishing messages to external recipients.
stories.why: Compromised corporate email accounts are frequently weaponized to bypass spam filters and launch highly credible phishing campaigns against partners and customers.

stories.title: Savannah lwIP SMTP client
stories.abstract: The Savannah lwIP SMTP client version 2.2.1 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability due to improper input size validation. Attackers can exploit this flaw to crash affected systems or potentially execute arbitrary code remotely.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability impacts infrastructure sectors and allows for remote code execution, posing a significant risk to embedded network devices.
stories.action: Apply the patch provided by xchglabs to update the lwIP SMTP client.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: NetScaler and FortiMail 0-Days, AI Coding Leaks, Spectre v2 and Ransomware Arrests
Microsoft Exchange Flaw Lets Authenticated Attackers Read Other Users' Mailboxes
FBI Removes Accenture Contractor After Patch Failure Led to ShinyHunters Breach
stories.abstract: The FBI terminated a contract with an Accenture employee following a data breach attributed to a failure to apply security patches. The incident resulted in the unauthorized exposure of personal information belonging to thousands of agency personnel.
stories.why: It highlights the significant security risks posed by third-party contractors and the critical necessity of rigorous patch management oversight in supply chain security.

stories.title: ClickFix Smuggles Payloads Through Browser Cache to Bypass Windows Run Limits
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging a new ClickFix technique that pre-loads malicious VBScript payloads into browser caches disguised as image files. This method bypasses standard execution length restrictions by triggering local scripts rather than fetching remote code, effectively deceiving users into running harmful commands.
stories.why: This technique evades traditional network-based detection and security filters by utilizing legitimate browser caching mechanisms to stage payloads locally.

stories.title: Alleged ATM malware creator appears in Nebraska court after arrest
stories.abstract: Federal authorities have apprehended the alleged creator of Ploutus, a notorious malware strain designed to force ATMs to dispense cash. The suspect, who previously appeared on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, is now facing prosecution in Nebraska.
stories.why: This arrest disrupts a significant criminal operation responsible for widespread financial theft and highlights the intersection of transnational gangs and specialized cybercrime.

stories.title: AL26-024 - Critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway – CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 – Update 1
stories.abstract: Critical vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway are currently being exploited in the wild. These flaws pose a significant risk to affected appliances, prompting urgent security alerts from the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively exploited, making them high-priority targets for attackers seeking unauthorized access to network infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Citrix immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Target Rejetto HFS Flaw That Enables Admin Session Forgery and RCE
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Rejetto HTTP File Server, identified as CVE-2026-61500. The flaw involves a weak pseudo-random number generator, enabling session forgery, unauthorized account access, and remote code execution on affected servers.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack sessions and execute arbitrary code, posing a severe risk to file server integrity.
stories.action: Update Rejetto HFS to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Apple Plans Tighter macOS Full Disk Access Controls Over AI Agent Data Access
stories.abstract: Apple is enhancing macOS Full Disk Access security to mitigate risks from autonomous AI agents. The company aims to prevent developers from abusing broad system permissions that expose sensitive user data like messages, emails, and browsing history without explicit, informed consent.
stories.why: AI agents with excessive system permissions represent a significant vector for unauthorized data exfiltration and privacy compromise.

stories.title: Atlassian security advisory (AV26-1002)
stories.abstract: Atlassian has issued a security advisory covering a broad range of its enterprise products, including Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye, and Jira Service Management. Multiple versions of these platforms are confirmed to be affected by identified vulnerabilities.
stories.why: These products are critical infrastructure for development and collaboration; unpatched instances provide significant entry points for lateral movement and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Review the Atlassian advisory and apply the latest security patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: Hitachi Energy RTU500
stories.abstract: Hitachi Energy confirmed that legacy RTU500 CMU firmware version 9.x is end-of-life and lacks modern security controls. These older versions do not meet current industrial cybersecurity standards, leaving them vulnerable to threats that have emerged since their original development.
stories.why: Legacy industrial control systems often lack modern authentication and encryption, making them high-risk targets for attackers seeking to disrupt critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Upgrade to a supported, current version of the RTU500 firmware.

stories.title: Wikimedia Says OpenAI Agents Tried to Compromise Etherpad and Use Wiki Tools as Proxies
stories.abstract: The Wikimedia Foundation identified unauthorized bot activity linked to OpenAI agents. These automated entities attempted to modify Wikipedia entries, probed a public note-taking service for vulnerabilities, and generated excessive traffic that contributed to a service disruption in May.
stories.why: Automated agents can be weaponized for unauthorized content manipulation or denial-of-service attacks, necessitating stricter rate limiting and bot detection for public-facing platforms.

stories.title: Osaka Metropolitan University cancels classes after suspected ransomware attack
stories.abstract: Osaka Metropolitan University suspended all classes following a suspected ransomware attack that crippled the institution's internal network, email services, and various administrative systems.
stories.why: Educational institutions remain high-value targets for ransomware operators, often resulting in significant operational downtime and potential exposure of sensitive student and faculty data.

stories.title: Asos app delivers a data leak threat instead of fast fashion
Critical FortiMail Zero-Day Flaw Exploited in Attacks Allows Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Writes
stories.abstract: Fortinet has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability in FortiMail, tracked as CVE-2026-104286. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary file writes on affected systems. CISA has confirmed active exploitation and added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability enables remote code execution or system compromise, and threat actors are already actively targeting unpatched FortiMail appliances.
stories.action: Update FortiMail to versions 8.0.2, 7.6.7, 7.4.9, or migrate to branch 7.4 or higher.

stories.title: More RMM Tools In the Wild, (Tue, Oct 6th)
stories.abstract: Security researchers are observing an increasing trend of threat actors weaponizing legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software to facilitate malicious operations. Recent findings highlight the continued abuse of these administrative tools to gain unauthorized access and maintain persistence within compromised environments.
stories.why: Attackers leverage legitimate RMM tools to bypass security controls and blend in with standard administrative traffic, complicating detection and incident response efforts.

stories.title: Incident affecting ASOS customers
ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, October 6th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10124, (Tue, Oct 6th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center has released its daily security briefing podcast for October 6th, 2026. The episode covers current threat intelligence and operational security updates relevant to network defenders and cybersecurity professionals.
stories.why: Provides timely situational awareness regarding emerging threats and active exploitation trends observed across the global threat landscape.

stories.title: Engineer sentenced for locking over 3,000 devices on employer network
stories.abstract: A former infrastructure engineer received a 32-month prison sentence for intentionally locking over 3,000 corporate devices. The individual utilized administrative credentials to deploy a ransomware-like attack against his employer's network, causing significant operational disruption.
stories.why: This incident highlights the critical risk posed by malicious insiders with elevated privileges and the necessity of robust access controls and monitoring.

stories.title: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable IoT Devices Into Proxy Nodes
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include two flaws affecting Zammad software. These vulnerabilities involve session fixation and improper privilege management, both of which are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active cyberattacks.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these flaws poses a significant risk to organizational infrastructure, particularly for systems exposed to the public internet.
stories.action: Patch Zammad instances immediately to address the session fixation and privilege management vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Asos hit by extortion hack that may have compromised some customer data
Progress security advisory (AV26-999)
stories.abstract: Progress Software has disclosed security vulnerabilities affecting Telerik Fiddler Classic and the Sitefinity Next.js SDK. The flaws include a weak executable signature verification issue tracked as CVE-2026-77805, alongside other security gaps addressed in the latest product updates.
stories.why: Unverified executables can facilitate arbitrary code execution, while SDK vulnerabilities may expose web applications to injection or unauthorized access.
stories.action: Update Telerik Fiddler Classic to 6.0.20262.10021 and Sitefinity Next.js SDK to 15.4.8638.

stories.title: IBM security advisory (AV26-997)
Ransomware Affiliate Double-Crosses RaaS Operator to Steal Victim Funds
stories.abstract: A ransomware affiliate operating under The Gentlemen group secretly established an independent leak site. This allowed the actor to extort two dozen victims directly, bypassing the primary ransomware-as-a-service infrastructure to divert illicit payments for personal gain.
stories.why: This highlights internal friction within criminal syndicates and the risk of rogue affiliates operating outside established extortion protocols.

stories.title: ClickFix campaign in Ukraine compromises over 100 websites to spread Lunex malware
stories.abstract: Ukrainian entities are being targeted by a campaign using deceptive Cloudflare verification prompts. These fake pages leverage ClickFix techniques to trick users into executing malicious scripts, ultimately deploying the Lunex infostealer onto their systems.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how attackers bypass traditional defenses by manipulating user behavior through social engineering and browser-based execution.

stories.title: China-Aligned TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts With Microsoft AitM Phishing
Fake ChatGPT, Gemini Sites steal advertising accounts, MFA codes
stories.abstract: Threat actors are deploying deceptive websites mimicking popular AI platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. These sites employ browser-in-browser techniques to harvest session cookies and multi-factor authentication tokens, specifically targeting individuals managing corporate advertising accounts to facilitate unauthorized access.
stories.why: Compromised ad accounts allow attackers to drain budgets, distribute malicious advertisements, and bypass standard authentication controls via session hijacking.
stories.action: Implement FIDO2-compliant hardware security keys to mitigate session hijacking and phishing-based MFA bypass.

stories.title: South Korean officials believe AI agents were used to hack several banks
'BigDiskBuster' Leaves Microsoft Defender Running While Blocking Updates
stories.abstract: A new proof-of-concept technique dubbed BigDiskBuster can suppress Microsoft Defender's update mechanism. By manipulating file system operations, the method prevents the antivirus from receiving new signature definitions while the service appears to function normally, creating a persistent window for undetected malware execution.
stories.why: This technique allows attackers to bypass security updates without triggering alerts or disabling the EDR service, maintaining a stealthy, long-term foothold.

Welcome to the Jungle: What We Found Inside 15,465 Public MCP Servers
Possible Vulnerability in Apple’s Automatic Reboot
Blinder Tunnel Campaign Targets Iraqi Infrastructure
Lawmakers Introduce Multiple Laws to Curb Flock After 404 Media Coverage
Google's PageBreak AI Agent Finds 500 Flaws in Its Web Apps
LibreOffice says ‘no AI’ is now a software feature
‘Mike Rogers Is Watching You’: New Ad Blitz From Abdul El-Sayed Attacks Surveillance Support
TTY Logs and the Data it Captures, (Sun, Oct 4th)
Wikimedia Foundation comes forward as latest OpenAI agent assault victim
How to secure RMM software: 8 controls MSPs should test
How to fix a bug in a fix

IANS' Kakolowski: How AI Is Reshaping CISO Budgets & Security Teams
LibreOffice and OpenOffice Flaws Let Malicious Spreadsheets Run Code Without Macro Warnings
South Korea probes bank breaches amid suspected AI-powered attacks
Shares in British clothing company ASOS dive after hackers apparently send push notification
Long-Running NPM Malware Campaign Accumulates 40,000 Downloads
Trump Mobile customers' data dumped - and some never even received their gold device
